claims.claim: Reviewers report that the combat system is clunky, frustrating, and heavily punishes players when facing multiple enemies.

citations.review_text:
The game itself is basically a typical open-world RPG with filled with unfun fetch quests and, of course, an unforgiving save system, because it's oh so realistic! The realism in this is poorly adapted, really. You get stuck in a river with Henry not being able to climb over the river bank, the NPC's behave weird in many situations...

The combat itself is interesting, but it seems it's mostly designed for 1v1 battles. As soon as you have to fight multiple people, you're pretty much done for. And that's the problem, most enemies scattered around in the world are at least two people who simply gang up on you. So you only need to randomly run into a band of bandits or Cumans and you can pretty load your last savegame from two hours ago or something. Escape is, at least to my experience, futile too. They can easily throw you off your horse too so don't think you can run them over which should be definitely possible in an oh so realistic game...

It can be fun but only for those with an extremely high tolerance threshold.

Extremely impressive (technically) but easily the LEAST enjoyable game I have ever spent my money on. I get that it's unrealistic to always win a fight against 5 enemies reliably, but I'm also not a fan of the "if you're outnumbered, you will die" mechanic in a game that limits how often you can save progress.

citation.review_text: Honestly... there are just too many bugs. From clothing, to being stuck in places, to dialogue bugs, time scheduling with quests, loading screen bugs, waiting with T and being stuck in that too. If you want to play Kingdom Come, play the 2nd one. This one just felt like a massive bug that never got fixed.

This game is undeniably great, but I have so many problems with it right now that it's basically unplayable.

I'll explain. Every 5 to 25 minutes, the game just crashes with one of the following errors: DXGI_ERROR_DEVICE_HUNG, DXGI_ERROR_DEVICE_REMOVED, or DXGI_ERROR_DEVICE_RESET. Every crash is also accompanied by an AMD Adrenalin driver timeout.

I have absolutely no idea why this is even happening. My PC is more than capable of handling this game, and I've already played KCD2 from beginning to end with zero issues.

The frustrating part is that I genuinely want to play and enjoy this game, but these constant crashes are making it almost impossible.

So, if anybody has any idea what's happening here or knows how to fix these issues, please let me know in the comments. I'd really appreciate the help!

[h1] Kingdom Come: Deliverance – A Portal to the Past [/h1]

I have a low-key regret of letting KCD sit in my Steam library for so long without giving it a proper chance.

I attempted to play it twice before finally sitting down and committing to it. The first time, I made it only as far as the fistfight with Kunesh during the prologue. The combat felt so weird and unfamiliar that I simply gave up. The second attempt came after a considerable gap. I made it as far as Talmberg Castle, but the night sequence absolutely tanked my FPS. It was clear that my old GTX 1660 Super was struggling.

Eventually, I upgraded my GPU and decided to give the game another shot, this time starting fresh. I didn't have any particular expectations. I just wanted to see what this game was actually about.

And boy, what a journey it turned out to be.

KCD is one of those games that takes time to get into, but once it clicks, it really grows on you. It demands patience, and more importantly, it asks you to unlearn almost everything you've learned from playing other RPGs. Its mechanics are different, its approach to progression is different, and its entire philosophy is different.

You're not some legendary warrior, a chosen one, or a supernatural being with extraordinary abilities. You're Henry, a blacksmith's son who knows practically nothing about the world beyond his little corner of Bohemia. The game takes you from there and puts you on a journey where you gradually learn, adapt, survive and eventually become a capable fighter.

And that's where KCD gets things so right. You're not just watching Henry grow; you're growing alongside him.

 [h2] The World [/h2]

The world is easily one of the game's biggest achievements. It feels alive, and not just because of its NPCs having their own day and night schedules. Settlements feel inhabited, people have their routines, and the countryside has a natural rhythm to it. There's something incredibly satisfying about simply travelling through Bohem…

claims.claim: Reviewers describe the combat system as clunky, challenging, and difficult to master, requiring significant time and practice to become proficient.

citations.review_text: This game has immense emotional and artistic significance for me. It is one of the first games that made me fall in love with medieval history and properly immersed me into a story focused, adventure and action-packed world. It helped me through an emotionally turbulent time, and will always have a special place in my heart. In spite of the perceived clunkiness, or jittery beginnings of Warhorse's first title, it is an immensely rich game, with beautiful landscapes, tailored npcs, side quests, activities and world building. Being based on the Sasau region of Bohemia (Czechia) with places like Pirkstein castle and Sasau monastery still being visitable today, it is incredible story of a passion project seen not just through the 1st act of Henry's story, but through everything around the game to make it an engaging almost holistic experience that no other game has come close to, maybe apart from Red Dead Redemption 2 or of course Kingdom Come: Deliverance II. For some people the combat can be tricky and it is obviously fairly outdated, but it is very unique within its combat mechanics and takes worthwhile time to become proficient, as it is part of the image and purpose of the game. You are not some all powerful character, Henry starts as just a numbskull, unskilled yokel who can't hold any weapons properly or communicate effectively at all. You get to build Henry into a beast who can take on any challenge. The only criticism I have is that compared to the second game, that is even more incredibly rich and ultimately streamlines and expands on what Kingdom Come is, thievery is way too overpowered. You can seriously abuse stealing everything from the armoury and swordsmith in Rattay, walk at a terribly slow pace as you'll be over-encumbered back to miller Peshek's place and sell him everything you stole, and about a week later of in game time, he'll have sold every single item and have the value in straight cash. I enjoyed and abused this mechanic, although it breaks im…

After completing the game and looking on the end credits, i couldn't do anything but have a big smile on my face. Story was amazing, characters were lovable, it had great script writing and it was a very funny game which i was not expecting. The only thing that i would warn about new players is the combat is VERY clunky. Getting jumped more then a couples guys could mean death if not careful. BUT i would more then likely play this games two or three times over just to experience more of the world and be immersed all over

This game has become one of my absolute most favorite games. Not gonna lie, It took a lot not to uninstall it 14 hours in to it. A lot of the mechanics were hard to get down, the story line was a bit hard to get into, and I flat out sucked at fighting. But let me tell ya, once I got some traction going, learned how to make money, how to fight better, how to brew potions, AND how to play AS Henry, I couldn't stop playing. Because of my work schedule it took me three months to beat this game, And it was worth every single bit of that time. 

The graphics kind of suck but overall 10/10.

The secret timed quest mechanic with Reeky was annoying. Guy was dead before I even set foot in Ledetchko to begin looking for him. Might not sound that game breaking, but it felt like the game was punishing me for exploring its world and not just rushing the main quest and that's just a minor gripe.

The Master Strike system might be one of the worst, most poorly thought out combat mechanics in gaming history. A master strike is a parry that allows you to get a free hit on an enemy if you time it just as the enemy swings. Sounds like great reward incentive for a skilled player, right? The problem is that the game lets enemies do it to you too and there is ZERO counter to it. The enemy just gets to hit you for free over and over again as if the game's trying to punish you just for trying to play it.

Many one on one duels are only winnable if you do nothing but just master strike the enemy over and over again. Master Strike, quick hit, back off. That's all you can do or else the enemy will start getting free hits on you if you try to do a combo. If you don't do that, the duel will turn into a gambling match of will the AI master strike every attack I make until I die or not?

That doesn't work for group fights since the enemy's allies can hit you while you master strike, so you have to rush them down one by one and hope they don't counter you every hit. There's no skilled gameplay anymore, it just becomes a game of chance. The only way to avoid this game of chance is to be grossly overleveled.

ALL of this could've been avoided if they had just not let the enemies counter you for free. Great mechanic for the player, mind bogglingly bad idea to let the enemy to do it too.

[h1][b]From Rags to Steel[/b][/h1]
[b]Kingdom Come: Deliverance[/b] is THE best historically accurate medieval game I have ever played. For the first game from Warhorse it is incredible how well it ended up considering it's struggles during development. While some mechanics and certain parts of the game can be clunky at times, the overall experience is absolutely amazing.

Probably the biggest gripe with this game for most people, the combat system. It ABSOLUTELY takes time to get used to, but once you start training and gaining some experience in fights you could REALISTICALLY win, you will see that it's supposed to be unfriendly in the beginning, but becomes almost second-nature the longer you play the game, which is exactly how becoming proficient in something works in real life. Another gripe is the saving mechanic requiring you to drink a specific item which is costly to buy or time-consuming to produce. I didn't like this at first either, but it definitely makes you think before doing something stupid, and if it really bothers you you could always get a mod to save whenever you want.

The graphics are great for the time. Not Red Dead Redemption 2 level of graphics but still beautiful, especially the nature, and that paired with the story makes for a great experience. In conclusion you should definitely give this game a try if you're into realistic RPGs or a medieval history nerd, and then try out the sequel since I've heard it's even better.

claims.claim: Reviewers report that the game lacks clear indicators for which quests or objectives are time-sensitive, leading to failed missions if exploration takes too long.

citations.review_text:
Kingdom Come: Deliverance is a realistic medieval RPG and one of the most immersive games I have ever played.
I wrote this review after finishing the second part.

[h2]Story & Quests[/h2]
The quest system is absolutely amazing. I have never seen one this elaborate and realistic in any other game.
You are not some chosen one, you are just a nobody, which is extremely refreshing.
Everything feels incredibly realistic, from your life decisions and how your character develops to whether you become a criminal or a hero.
Side quests develop organically and often surprise you. You help someone for a moment and suddenly you find yourself in a huge questline.
Most quests do not just have one or two solutions, there are often dozens of ways to solve them, some of them not even obvious. You can sometimes even do things before a quest actually starts and change the outcome that way, for example by killing someone in advance.
The downside is that there is no real indicator which quests are time based and which are not. I completely messed up the plague quest because it started while I was fast traveling and I did not even notice it.
The same goes for timed decisions in dialogues. If you need a bit longer to read or like to think things through, they are extremely annoying.
The story ends on a cliffhanger, so you will definitely want to play the second part right away.

[h2]World & NPCs[/h2]
The world feels extremely realistic and the historical accuracy is on a level that hardly any other game reaches.
The NPCs live their own lives and even talk to each other about things that happened, which makes the world feel truly alive.
The towns are all medium sized and very individual, and there are plenty of points of interest and random encounters to discover.
The day and night cycle also matters a lot since many mechanics depend on the time of day.
The music gives you real medieval vibes and fits the game perfectly.

[h2]Character Progression[/h2]
You start as an uneducated blacksmith…

[i]Kingdom Come: Deliverance[/i] sits somewhere between a medieval life simulator and an action RPG, and it manages to balance these two aspects remarkably well.

One of the biggest challenges facing open-world RPGs is making the main story feel urgent while allowing the player to freely explore the world and pursue side quests. [i]Kingdom Come: Deliverance[/i] handles this surprisingly well by building its main narrative around a quest for revenge without imposing a rigid timeline on the player. You can advance the main story whenever you feel like it, making the experience feel much more natural. At its heart, this is also a coming-of-age story about Henry and his transformation from an inexperienced young man into someone capable of navigating the harsh realities of medieval life.

I highly recommend completing the side quests you come across, and not just because they help develop Henry's character. The quests are varied, explore different aspects of everyday life in medieval Bohemia, and feature excellent writing and entertaining character interactions. You'll find yourself doing everything from navigating dark mine shafts to helping the local executioner sabotage a rival's work. There are plenty of laughs along the way, too.

A word of advice for fellow completionists: while the main story quests aren't timed in the same way as certain side quests, some side missions have time-sensitive objectives, and taking too long can affect their outcomes. If you don't want to risk missing content, the [i]Timed Quest Indicator[/i] mod is well worth installing.

The simulation mechanics are engaging, although they can occasionally become tedious. Alchemy, for example, is an interesting activity at first, but brewing potions gets repetitive after a while. The saving system can also be unforgiving, as saving your progress regularly requires Saviour Schnapps. Since saving is effectively a resource, you'll naturally adopt a more cautious playstyle. Still, there were se…

Perhaps the most frustrating game I've ever played. Uncountable number of poor design decisions on gameplay that frequently left me wondering why I'm spending my time on this just to feel angry and dissatisfied after leaving. Quests that are designed to be failed without any indication to player, unclear objectives, overly harsh combat at some points, a save system that only really works for a game that doesn't need to be save-scummed a few dozen times because of bugs.

However I kept coming back anyways, enough to finish the game and DLC (outside of a few side quests and the Theresa DLC). This game is graphically and artistically beautiful, good story, and culturally immersive. The combat does shine in some areas and the role-playing elements are overall well-designed and numerous. Truly a piece of art through and through.

After finishing, I wasn't sure whether I would tell my past self to play this game if I could go back in time. I'm now midway through the sequel, which has made any doubts about having played this one vanish. Would recommend, with the asterisk that it will be frustrating and to not be afraid to look up issues rather than assume you're just not good enough.

[h1]Not exactly bad, but definitely lacking in many aspects – a pretentious review[/h1]

[h2]My biggest grievance: Lock-picking[/h2]
it is impossible to do even the tutorial lock. What the game fails to tell you is that you need to pay for training first to have any chance at opening even the tutorial lock. Lock difficulties straight up lie to you too, so "very easy" just means that a low skill Henry can attempt it, not that it will actually be easy to pick. In the end I had to get a mod that make the lock picking a bit easier, but it still wasn't a cake walk. Whoever designed this mini-game, and whoever approved it should be banned from the games industry for life.

[h2]It is in general unpolished[/h2]
especially quests are very lacking. I did some things in a way the game clearly did not expect and I received dialogue referencing events that did not occur.

[h2]Voice acting[/h2]
(Played in English): the Nobles are greatly cast and acted, but pretty much every other NPC is stiff as a board, has strange intonation not matching what they are saying. In many dialogues there is a 2 second pause when someone "interrupts" someone else. Audio quality is also unacceptably bad, the "high quality audio DLC" is only a minor improvement.

[h2]Music[/h2]
it is fine, but gets annoying when the same 'jingle' plays for the 10th time in as many minutes.

[h2]Saving[/h2]
I get that this is a "hardcore" game, but it is unacceptable, this system is discriminatory against people who have lives, another thing I had to change with a mod

[h2]Story[/h2]
for me is a mostly good mixed bag. There are times when Henry as a protagonist is absolutely unbearable, especially in the prologue and early game. Otherwise it is a bit contrived but generally interesting plot.

[h2]Combat was a mixed bag too[/h2]
I like the directional aspect but it strays a bit close to QTEs which I do despise. Master-strikes also trivialize the whole mechanic a little bit. The system was also clearly built for duels, b…

[h1][b]From Rags to Steel[/b][/h1]
[b]Kingdom Come: Deliverance[/b] is THE best historically accurate medieval game I have ever played. For the first game from Warhorse it is incredible how well it ended up considering it's struggles during development. While some mechanics and certain parts of the game can be clunky at times, the overall experience is absolutely amazing.

Probably the biggest gripe with this game for most people, the combat system. It ABSOLUTELY takes time to get used to, but once you start training and gaining some experience in fights you could REALISTICALLY win, you will see that it's supposed to be unfriendly in the beginning, but becomes almost second-nature the longer you play the game, which is exactly how becoming proficient in something works in real life. Another gripe is the saving mechanic requiring you to drink a specific item which is costly to buy or time-consuming to produce. I didn't like this at first either, but it definitely makes you think before doing something stupid, and if it really bothers you you could always get a mod to save whenever you want.

The graphics are great for the time. Not Red Dead Redemption 2 level of graphics but still beautiful, especially the nature, and that paired with the story makes for a great experience. In conclusion you should definitely give this game a try if you're into realistic RPGs or a medieval history nerd, and then try out the sequel since I've heard it's even better.

Kingdom Come Deliverance is one of the greatest RPGs ever made. It’s a diamond in the rough. Sure, it has far too many bugs and runs terribly even on high-end hardware, to the point where the second game looks better in virtually every way while running significantly faster. But even with all its flaws, the original remains one of the most creative and unique RPGs in decades.

The world is simply impeccable. It looks beautiful and features some of the most realistic natural environments in gaming, surpassed only by the sequel. The story is fantastic, filled with memorable characters, plenty of funny moments, and genuinely heartfelt scenes that make the journey feel special.

As an archaeology student with a deep love for the Middle Ages, what impresses me most is how convincingly the game portrays medieval society. Despite being a work of fiction, it captures the atmosphere, culture, and everyday realities of the period in a way that Hollywood productions rarely manage. Of course, it takes some creative liberties where necessary, but its historical authenticity is remarkable.

The churches are a particular highlight. Almost every settlement has one, and each seems more beautifully decorated than the last, with stunning frescoes, elaborate altars, and golden ornaments. Exploring these sacred spaces is a joy in itself, and they do a fantastic job of bringing medieval religious life to the screen.

My main complaints, aside from the poor optimization and technical instability, concern the combat system. While it is revolutionary in its ambition and, contrary to what many critics claim, not nearly as difficult as people make it out to be, it can feel incredibly clunky. Worse still, the system completely falls apart during group fights, which can turn otherwise exciting encounters into frustrating experiences.

Nevertheless, Kingdom Come Deliverance will always be one of my favorite RPGs of all time. It’s an ambitious, deeply immersive, and wonderfully unique experience …

claims.claim: Reviewers mention encountering physics jank, broken AI behavior, and occasional bugs that require consulting online guides to resolve.

citations.review_text: This was one of the best RPGs I have ever played. Absolutely phenomenal, even at release. And I'm saying that not despite of, but inclusive of all the physics jank. Don't get me wrong, if you haven't played this and are into RPGs, just get it. You won't be disappointed. But honestly what sticks in my mind are the antics of the (sometimes) broken AI and physics. One memorable glitch was in the village of Father Morton. All the NPCs of the village seemed to be stuck in an invisible hole in the floor, and were bubbling in and out of it like lava. One would occasionally break free and would walk past me "Hail!". I went over to investigate, fell through the hole and out of the game world, watching the feet of the NPCs disappear to a speck above me. Absolute comedy. Or, once in the arena, when, just between a cut scene and a battle, literally every one of the hundred or so NPCs said in unison in a massive chorus "Henry's come to see us!" before I was beaten senseless. Or the typical conga line of guards in stealth, in the middle of daylight as a roaming chicken runs across in front of them. Or, just as I'm about to get into a fight with a guy (coming out of dialog), "well met!". Then you proceed to beat the s***e out of each other. Again, you can't make this up, and for me, it turned it into one of the most memorable games I have ever played precisely BECAUSE of its jank.

A great game, really best in class at what it does. There are still issues - some jank, occasional bug that requires heading to Google to sort out, and tasks that require you follow painfully slow NPCs - but the sword fighting is great, the story is solid, and the world seems alive and is genuinely enjoyable to inhabit. Recommend.
